comment: Tribal land and boundary records from the BIA's ArcGIS portal: layer, name, state, area, and geometry. A 100-row probe. FIPS and geometry columns make it joinable to county tables once fully poured.
County-level quarterly and annual employment and wage statistics by industry (NAICS) and ownership sector, derived from unemployment insurance tax records.

Aggregate federal inmate and facility statistics published by BOP, landed as metric rows (category, metric, value, date). Small reference table -- good for topline context like population trends, not individual-level analysis.

CBP's nationwide encounter numbers landed in spreadsheet shape: one row per category with months as columns (OCT_25, NOV_25...). Nine rows -- usable for a quick topline but the pivoted layout fights SQL; the OHSS monthly table on this shelf is the better-shaped source.

CDC's Household Pulse tracker of mental-health symptoms: the estimated share of adults reporting anxiety or depression, broken out by state and by subgroup (age, race, gender, etc.) across survey periods since 2020. Includes confidence intervals so you can judge how solid each estimate is. Raw landing table -- every value stored as text, and these are survey-based estimates with margins of error, not exact counts. Cast VALUE before charting trends.

Indicator-level records pulled from data.cdc.gov spanning vaccinations, chronic disease, outbreaks, and environmental health: indicator, state/FIPS/ZIP, year, and value. A broad sampler of CDC's portal rather than one deep dataset -- good for quick health context by place.

The CDC's county-level overdose death rates -- the map layer of the drug-death crisis, showing which counties got worse and when. Keyed by county FIPS, so it joins to almost any US geographic data. Heads up: the raw death rate here is banded into ranges (a text bucket, not an exact number) to protect small-county privacy -- fine for mapping hotspots, not for precise counts. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

CDC survey indicators of health insurance coverage: the share of people insured, broken out by state, demographic subgroup, and time period, with confidence intervals. Tracks who has coverage and who doesn't across the country. These are survey estimates, not headcounts, so read them with the intervals. Raw landing, stored as text; 16,056 rows from CDC NCHS.

CDC estimates of death and injury rates for each US county, broken out by intent (suicide, homicide, unintentional, etc.) -- the county-level picture of overdose and gun violence. Rates come with margins of error, and small counts are suppressed for privacy. Raw as loaded (all text); GEOID is the county FIPS code -- your join to any other county data. From CDC.

CDC's provisional count of U.S. drug-overdose deaths: rows by state, year/month, and indicator (total, or a specific drug class like fentanyl or heroin). Because it's provisional, it also carries how complete the data is and a predicted value that adjusts for reporting lag. This is the running body count of the overdose epidemic. Raw landing table -- values stored as text, and 'provisional' means recent months will revise upward as investigations close.

The CDC's official suicide death rates for the US, sliced by year, age group, sex and race/ethnicity. Good for tracking how suicide has moved over decades and which groups are hit hardest. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text) -- ESTIMATE is a rate, not a count, and rows carry demographic-breakdown labels (STUB_NAME/STUB_LABEL) you filter on. No geography and no join keys, so it stands alone as a trend source.

Home Mortgage Disclosure Act records: one row per mortgage application with lender (LEI), census tract, borrower demographics, loan terms, and outcome. The landed 28K rows are a sample of an enormous annual release. This is the canonical dataset for lending-discrimination analysis -- census tract joins it to redlining maps and demographics.

CISA's authoritative catalog of software vulnerabilities (CVEs) with real evidence of active in-the-wild attacks -- which vendor and product, what it does, whether it's been used in ransomware, and the federal deadline to patch it. The short list of flaws that actually matter right now. Raw as loaded (all text); keyed by CVE_ID. From CISA.

The public registry of clinical studies from ClinicalTrials.gov: each trial's sponsor, the drug or device tested, the condition, the phase, enrollment, and crucially whether (and how late) results ever got posted. Great for spotting sponsors who bury results. Carries an NPI so trials can point back to real providers. Heads up: this is a thin 500-row sample, good for exploring the shape, not for counting the full registry.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

All 7,557 Medicare-certified dialysis facilities from CMS Care Compare -- location, ownership (for-profit vs non-profit, and the chain that owns it), star rating, and outcome measures like patient mortality, hospitalization, infection, and transfusion rates. Keyed by CCN, so it joins to other CMS provider data. Great for asking whether for-profit or chain-owned centers have worse patient outcomes. Raw landing, all text.

The bridge between individual clinicians and the facilities they practice at: 2.2 million rows linking a doctor's NPI to a facility's CCN. This is the crosswalk that lets you follow a named doctor to the hospitals, nursing homes, and dialysis centers they're tied to. Keyed by both NPI and CCN -- rare and valuable connective tissue. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

The yearly financial and operational filing every Medicare-participating hospital must submit to CMS -- one row per hospital per fiscal year with hundreds of fields: revenue, total costs, assets and liabilities, bed counts, staffing, charity and uncompensated care, and profit margins. This is how you follow the money inside a hospital's books. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by CCN, also carries NPI, name, address, ZIP; ~6,103 rows.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

All 12,392 home health agencies certified by Medicare, with services offered, ownership, star ratings, and dozens of patient-outcome measures (how often patients got better, Medicare spending per episode). One row per agency, keyed by CCN so it joins to billing and ownership. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

All 6,852 hospice providers certified by Medicare, with location, ownership type, and certification date. One row per hospice, keyed by CCN (the Medicare facility ID) so it joins to billing, ownership, and quality data. The end-of-life care leg of the CMS provider spine. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

The CMS Provider Data Catalog (Hospital Compare) hospital roster: facility ID, name, address, type, ownership, and quality/safety designations. The most-connected table in the whole Library -- name+ZIP matches tie it to cost reports, provider files, and enforcement tables. Start here for anything hospital-shaped.

All 5,432 hospitals in the Medicare system, with type, ownership, whether they have an ER, overall quality rating, and counts of how they score on mortality, safety, and readmissions. One row per hospital, keyed by CCN so it joins to billing, ownership, and the rest of the provider spine. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

Meant to hold hospital standard charges -- gross, cash, and payer-negotiated prices -- from CMS-mandated machine-readable files. One row landed: a schema probe of the template. The real files are per-hospital and huge; this needs its own targeted pour.

All 1,222 inpatient rehabilitation facilities certified by Medicare (where patients recover after strokes, injuries, or surgery), with location, ownership type, and certification date. One row per facility, keyed by CCN so it joins to billing, ownership, and quality data. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

All 311 long-term care hospitals certified by Medicare (facilities treating patients who need extended hospital-level care), with location, ownership type, bed count, and certification date. One row per hospital, keyed by CCN so it joins to billing, ownership, and quality data. Raw landing table, values stored as text.
The catalog of what data.cms.gov offers: dataset titles, descriptions, formats, and URLs. A finding aid for Medicare/Medicaid data worth pouring individually -- the shopping list, not the groceries.

One row per provider per year showing what they billed Medicare: services rendered, patients seen, charges submitted, and dollars Medicare actually paid, plus patient demographics and chronic-condition mix. 1.3M rows keyed by NPI, so it joins to the provider spine, pharma payments, and the banned-provider list. Raw landing -- every value is text, cast dollar amounts before you sum them.

The real acquisition cost of drugs (CMS NADAC): what pharmacies actually pay per unit for each drug, identified by NDC, with the drug description, pricing unit, brand/generic flag, and the matching generic's cost. 1.5M rows. Cross it against what Medicare/Medicaid reimburse and you find the markup -- where the overpayment story lives. NDC is the steel join key to FDA drug data, Part D, and RxNorm. Raw landing table: every value stored as text, so cast prices and dates before comparing.

Every active healthcare provider in America with an NPI number -- 9.6 million doctors, nurses, clinics, hospitals, and organizations -- with names, addresses, specialties (taxonomy), and license numbers. This is the spine of the health data: payments, bans, and Medicare billing all point back to a provider here. Keyed by NPI, with EIN, name, and ZIP for further joins. If a provider exists, they're in this table. Published monthly by CMS.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

One row per certified nursing home from CMS Care Compare -- overall and category star ratings, staffing hours per resident, ownership and chain, inspection deficiencies, fines, payment denials, and an abuse-icon flag. This is the go-to for spotting understaffed or repeatedly-cited facilities and tracing them up to their parent chains. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by CCN plus NPI, county FIPS, lat/lon, name, address, ZIP; ~14,700 rows.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

CMS Open Payments general-payments detail: 15.4M individual payments and gifts from drug and device companies to physicians and teaching hospitals -- who paid, who got it (with NPI), how much, what it was for (meals, travel, consulting, speaking), and the drug or device involved. Cross it with Medicare prescribing to see whether the money moves the pen. Raw landing, all text -- cast the dollar amount before summing.
CMS Open Payments - General Payments Detail (PY2022)

CMS Open Payments for 2023: each general payment or gift from a pharma/device company to a physician or teaching hospital -- amount, date, the company, and the drug or device it was tied to (14.7M rows). This is how you see which doctors take money from whom. Carries NPI (doctor) and CCN (hospital) so it links to the provider spine and the banned-provider list. Raw landing -- every field text, one program year (2023) only.

One row per prescriber showing their Medicare Part D prescribing: total claims, drug cost, day supply, brand vs generic split, and dedicated opioid and antibiotic measures including opioid prescribing rate. 1.4M rows keyed by NPI. Pair it with pharma payments to test whether industry money tracks with what doctors prescribe. Raw landing, all text.

CMS Provider of Services file: the deep-detail record for ~44,000 hospitals and non-hospital facilities, with hundreds of columns on bed counts, staffing, services offered, ownership changes, and termination status. Keyed by CCN and carrying FIPS geography, it's the backbone reference for what a Medicare facility actually is and does. Raw landing table, values stored as text -- and yes, the column names are cryptic CMS codes.

Current committee and subcommittee membership for Congress: which member sits on or chairs which committee, with their party, rank, and role. 3,879 rows keyed by BIOGUIDE, so it joins straight to the member spine -- letting you connect a lawmaker's committee power to the industries donating to them. Raw landing, all text.

Every current and historical member of Congress (plus presidents/VPs): name, party, state, district, terms, and birthday. The keystone: it carries the master ID crosswalk (bioguide, icpsr, fec, opensecrets, govtrack, votesmart, wikidata, and more) so a legislator here links to their votes, their money, and their bio anywhere. Raw landing, stored as text; 12,847 rows spanning all of US history.

Catalog records from the David Rumsey Historical Map Collection with IIIF links to the actual map images. Ten items landed as a probe of the API shape. When a story needs 'what did this place look like in 1885', this is the finding aid.

Item-level metadata from the Densho Digital Repository documenting the WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans: object type, facility, narrator, topic, and rights. A 25-item probe of a much larger archive; complements the NARA internment records already on this shelf.

Monthly operational statistics from DHS's Office of Homeland Security Statistics: encounter type, region/sector, citizenship, family status, criminality, and outcomes. The most granular public view of border and interior enforcement -- the numbers behind every enforcement-surge story.

Rows from the DHS Yearbook of Immigration Statistics: category, fiscal year, country, and count across lawful permanent residents, admissions, refugees, and enforcement. A 27-row probe of the yearbook's tables -- historical context, decades deep once fully poured.

Text-mining-ready records from UNC's DocSouth collections: title, author, publication date, collection, and links to plain text and TEI/XML. 144 works including first-person slave narratives -- primary-source text for historical NLP work.

Meant to be the DOJ Civil Rights Division's cases and settlements -- housing, voting, disability, employment, police -- with who, what section, status and a link to the filing. But this landing table has only 1 row, so it's a placeholder/failed pull, good only for seeing the intended shape, not for counting or research. Raw text landing; re-ingest before trusting it.

A snapshot of every file link the DOJ's public Epstein Library page lists -- names, URLs, link text, and source page. Metadata only, never the documents themselves. Taken over time, snapshots reveal what appeared, what vanished, and what changed on the government's page. Only 777 rows, no join keys. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

DOJ False Claims Act settlements -- defendant, amount, qui tam / relator, fraud type, agency defrauded, district. Recovered from landing (was frozen at 12 rows).  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Annual Form 5500 filings: plan name, sponsor and its EIN, plan year, participant counts, and plan type for employer retirement/welfare plans. The sponsor EIN column is gold -- it hard-joins employers to the nonprofit master file, SEC filers, and anything else EIN-keyed.

Case-level foreign labor certification disclosures from DOL: employer name, job title, SOC code, wage, visa class, and case outcome. 665K rows and one of the most-connected tables in the Library -- employer names match to companies, and it's the definitive 'who sponsors foreign workers, for what jobs, at what pay' table.
The catalog of what BTS TranStats offers across transport modes: database name, mode, subject, and profile links. A finding aid for targeted pours (on-time performance, T-100 traffic, etc.).

The federal Election Administration and Voting Survey, one row per local election jurisdiction: voter registration counts, absentee/mail ballot volumes, provisional ballots, polling places, and poll-worker numbers. Column names are survey question codes (A1a, B2c...) -- you'll want the EAVS codebook open when you query it. FIPS codes join it to any county-level table.

EDFacts collects assessment proficiency, enrollment, and program participation from every state education agency, down to school level. Only a 33-row probe landed so far -- schema visible, data thin. Re-pour before drawing conclusions.

EOIR's FOIA-released immigration court database landed 12.6 million rows but only a single data column (case type) plus bookkeeping -- the wide file didn't survive the pour. The row count looks impressive and means almost nothing yet. Re-pour before touching it in any analysis.

EPA's ECHO file: 3.2 million regulated facilities and their enforcement record -- inspections, violations, penalties, and compliance status across air, water, waste, and drinking-water programs. Cross it with who's getting fined vs. who keeps polluting and you find where enforcement breaks down. Carries lat/lon and FIPS for spatial joins. Raw landing table, values stored as text.
A four-row probe of the FAA data portal's catalog -- dataset names and URLs only. A pointer list at best; the registry and safety data land separately.

Every US-registered civil aircraft: N-number, serial, make/model, year, and the registrant's name and address. The 'who owns that plane' table -- owner names and addresses match to companies and people across the Library, and it pairs naturally with flight-tracking work.

Foreign Agents Registration Act disclosures: registrant, foreign principal and its country, registration dates, and receipts/disbursements. Only a 30-row probe so far, but this is a marquee accountability source -- lobbyists for foreign powers, on the record. Worth a full pour.

The Foreign Agents Registration Act filings: everyone required to disclose they're working in the US on behalf of a foreign government, party, or company -- the registrant, the foreign principal, and the country behind it. 21,326 rows from DOJ bulk data, cleaned. This is how you see which foreign powers are paying US lobbyists and PR firms. Keyed by name, address, ZIP, and country.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

State-by-month counts of FBI firearm background checks, broken out by 24 check types (handgun, long gun, permit, pawn, private sale, etc.). The cleanest available signal for gun demand -- but a check is NOT a sale: permit rechecks and CCW renewals inflate the totals, so treat it as a proxy. Raw as loaded (all text); join on state name (map to FIPS in staging). FBI via the Data Liberation Project mirror.

The FCC Universal Licensing System: every radio station and wireless license, with call sign, licensee entity name, FRN, service code, and license status/dates. 1.7 million rows. Entity names and FRNs make it a solid who-operates-what lookup -- from ham radio to broadcast empires.

FDIC enforcement decisions and orders against banks, companies, and individuals -- cease-and-desist orders, money penalties, and removal/prohibition orders. Heads up: this is a thin 14-row sample, just the raw order text and URL, not the full enforcement database -- good for seeing the shape of the data, not for counting or analysis. Raw landing, stored as text.

Every FDIC-insured bank failure since 1934 (3,584 of them), one row per collapsed bank. Shows the bank's name and location, the failure date, how long it was insured before dying, the institution that acquired it, and the estimated loss to the federal deposit-insurance fund -- plus assets, deposits, and loss ratios. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by FDIC cert number and county FIPS so you can map failures geographically or tie them to the acquiring bank. The raw follow-the-collapse record for financial crises.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

The FEC committee master: 20,938 registered committees for the 2024 cycle -- name, treasurer, address, type (PAC, party, candidate committee), party affiliation, and any connected organization. Keyed by FEC_CMTE_ID (and FEC_CAND_ID where a committee is tied to a candidate), so it's the lookup that turns cryptic committee codes in the donation firehose into real names. Raw landing, all text.

The FEC candidate master: one row per registered federal candidate per cycle (17,900 rows) -- FEC candidate ID, name, office sought, party, state, district, and incumbent/challenger/open-seat status. The anchor that ties a candidate ID to a name and office across the whole money-in-politics stack. Links to committees and donations via CAND_ID. Raw text landing (FEC bulk cn.txt).

Every committee registered with the FEC for the 2026 cycle: committee ID, name, treasurer, address, type, party, and the candidate it's linked to. This is the committee dimension that candidate-to-money links resolve against. Landed alongside the 2024 committee master to close a 2026 gap (2026 linkages resolved only ~57% before this vs. ~98% for 2024). Keyed by FEC committee ID and candidate ID. Raw landing, stored as text; 20,007 rows.

The FEC candidate-to-committee linkage table (ccl.txt): 16,327 rows connecting each candidate ID to the committee IDs authorized by or linked to them, with committee type and designation. This is the clean join that lets you roll individual donations up from a committee to the actual candidate who benefits. Raw landing, all text.

One row per federal candidate per election cycle: total money raised, total spent, cash on hand, individual contributions, loans, and debts. This is the ONLY FEC bulk file that carries dollar amounts, so it's the source of every 'candidate raised $X' number. Keyed by FEC candidate ID (CAND_ID) to link back to the campaigns and committees. Raw landing, values stored as text; 7,933 rows.

Committee-to-candidate transactions: PAC and party contributions, plus independent expenditures for or against a candidate, one row each (866,730 rows) with amount, date and transaction type. The organized-money leg of follow-the-money in politics. Carries both CMTE_ID (the committee) and CAND_ID (the candidate) so it links committees to candidates by cycle. Raw text landing (FEC bulk pas2).

Every itemized individual contribution (over $200 aggregate) to a federal committee -- donor name, city/state/ZIP, free-text employer and occupation, amount, date, recipient committee, and the conduit for earmarked gifts. 84.2M rows across the 2024 and 2026 cycles. Gotcha: there's no cycle column (two files were merged), so derive the cycle from TRANSACTION_DT (MMDDYYYY). Raw landing, all text -- cast the amount before summing.

US Federal Register documents -- rules, notices, proclamations, executive orders with agencies, citations, dates, URLs. Recovered from landing (was LIMIT-capped at 5,000). document_number is the key.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

FFIEC Call Report data: the balance sheet and income statement every US commercial bank files quarterly, with total assets, deposits, past-due loans, and Tier 1 capital. A 302-row probe so far. RSSD ID joins it to FDIC bank data; watch a bank's past-dues climb before it fails.

The authoritative US house-price index from the FHFA, tracking how home prices move over time at every geography down to census tract. The price half of housing affordability -- joins by FIPS/ZIP onto redlining, census, and rent data. Heads up: values are unitless index numbers (not dollars) with different base years per series, and the file mixes geographic levels and index types in one table -- split and base-note it before use. Raw landing, stored as text; 184,807 rows.
Aggregate statistics on new, outstanding, and performance characteristics of US residential mortgages drawn from the NMDB 5% national sample, published at national, regional, state, and metro levels.

The Corporate Transparency Act registry of who actually owns companies, as filed with FinCEN. One row landed, and the March 2025 rule change exempted US domestic companies entirely -- so even the real feed only covers foreign reporting companies now. A stub with a shrunken mandate; keep expectations low.

The authoritative directory of all 4,067 federal judges (district, circuit, Supreme Court) from 1789 to today: name, demographics, birth/death, plus who nominated them, the appointing president's party, ABA rating, and confirmation vote for up to six appointments each. The backbone dimension for the judiciary. Keyed on the FJC nid. Raw landing -- wide, text-as-loaded, one column set per appointment.

One row per judgeship appointment for every Article III federal judge (4,766 rows): the court, the appointing president and their party, nomination and confirmation dates, the Senate Ayes/Nays, ABA rating, and when service ended. This is how you trace who put a judge on the bench and how contested it was. Keyed by the FJC judge NID. Raw text landing (Federal Judicial Center).

Every disbursement and obligation of US foreign assistance from ForeignAssistance.gov -- 4 million transactions with country, managing agency, sector, and dollar amounts by fiscal year. This is the ledger of where American aid money actually went.
Meant to hold railroad accident/incident reports: railroad, date, location, type, casualties, and cause. One row landed -- schema probe only. Re-pour before use.

Federal Trade Commission enforcement matters: who the FTC went after, when, for what (consumer protection vs. antitrust), and where the case stands. Respondent names and EINs make it matchable against company tables -- the 'has this company been in trouble before' lookup.

Official status records for 36,465 congressional measures: bill number, sponsor, cosponsor list, full action history, and a flag (with public-law number) for the ones that actually became law. Sponsor and cosponsors carry bioguide IDs, so it joins cleanly to the member roster -- follow a lawmaker to everything they've pushed. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

The official GovInfo cosponsor list flattened to one row per (bill, cosponsor): the member's bioguide id, party, state, whether they were an original cosponsor, the date they signed on, and the date they withdrew (if they did). Shows who backed what and who quietly pulled support. Keyed by member BIOGUIDE. Raw landing, stored as text.

Grant opportunity listings pulled from the Grants.gov search API: which agency is offering money, for what category, who's eligible, and whether it's still open. Only a 100-row probe has landed so far -- treat it as a working sample of the feed, not the full universe of open grants.

Every individual and entity currently excluded from Medicare, Medicaid and other federal health programs (83,464 rows), with the exclusion type and the date it started. Cross it with who's still getting paid and you find money going where it shouldn't. Keyed by NPI plus name/address/EIN, so it joins straight to the provider and payment tables. Raw landing (HHS Office of Inspector General) -- values stored as text.

HHS TAGGS grant awards -- award number, recipient (name/EIN/geo), amount, assistance-listing (CFDA) number. recipient_ein + recipient_fips are join keys; kept as text (leading zeros).  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Every Health Professional Shortage Area and Medically Underserved Area designation: discipline (primary care, dental, mental health), shortage score, status, and dates. Heavily geographic -- it link-matches to dozens of place-keyed tables and answers 'is this an underserved area?' for any US location.

A catalog of HUD Policy Development & Research datasets: name, URL, description, and rough geography columns. It's the shopping list, not the groceries -- 77 pointers to housing datasets worth pouring individually.

Quarterly ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations statistics: metric, fiscal quarter, country of citizenship, criminal-history category, and area of responsibility. Aggregate-level (221 rows) -- topline context that pairs with the bigger BORDER_ENFORCEMENT_MONTHLY table.

Return-level index of electronically filed IRS Form 990s: EIN, organization, tax period, gross receipts, total revenue/expenses/assets. A 200-row probe of the bulk XML universe. EIN joins it straight to the 3.9M-row tax-exempt master file on this shelf -- the index says who filed, the BMF says who exists.

The IRS Business Master File: the full roster of US tax-exempt orgs (1,974,830 rows) -- EIN, name, address, NTEE category code, subsection/foundation status, and assets/income/revenue. The IRS side of the EIN bridge, so it links nonprofits to donations, contracts and the banned lists by EIN. Concatenated from the 4 regional extracts. Raw text landing (IRS) -- every value stored as text.

The IRS auto-revocation list: 1.2M nonprofits stripped of tax-exempt status (usually for failing to file for three straight years), with the revocation date and any later reinstatement. Keyed by EIN, so you can check whether an org still soliciting donations or receiving grants is actually a revoked shell. Raw landing -- every value is text.

Aggregated tax-return statistics from the IRS SOI program at ZIP-code level: number of returns, income bracket (AGI stub), joint filers, exemptions, and more. This is the closest public thing to 'how much money lives in this ZIP' -- a natural denominator for any per-place analysis.

Every neighborhood the government's Home Owners' Loan Corporation graded from A ('best') to D ('hazardous') between 1935-1940 -- roughly 1,155 areas across ~200 cities, digitized and mapped by lat/lon and FIPS. The area descriptions spell out the reasoning, often explicitly racial, that steered mortgage money away from Black and immigrant neighborhoods. Join it to today's health, wealth, and lending data to trace how a line drawn 90 years ago still shows up. Georeferenced by University of Richmond from the original HOLC records.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

District-level US House general-election returns, one row per candidate per district per year (29,636 rows): votes, total votes, party, and special/runoff flags. The cleaned 'who won the House' source. Keyed by state FIPS + district; the winner links to the member spine by name+state+district (fuzzy -- no FEC ID in the file). Raw text landing (MIT Election Data + Science Lab).

State-level US presidential election results: one row per candidate per state per year, with votes for that candidate and total votes cast. This is the 'who won each state' geographic layer. Keyed by state FIPS so it joins to census and other geographic data -- but note the president is not in the Congress ID spine, so no member-of-Congress link. Raw landing, stored as text; 3,740 rows.

State-level Senate general-election returns, one row per candidate per race per year (3,945 rows): votes, total votes, party, plus flags for special elections and runoffs. The cleaned canonical 'who won the Senate' source. Keyed by state FIPS; the winner links to the member spine by name+state (fuzzy -- no FEC ID in the file). Raw text landing (MIT Election Data + Science Lab).

NAAG multistate settlements -- one row per multistate AG settlement (defendants, amounts, participating states, issue area, NAICS). Amounts kept as text (may carry currency formatting); cast in staging later.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

An index of selected historical electronic records from NARA's Access to Archival Databases -- dataset and series titles, record IDs, dates, person names, and locations across military, diplomatic, and personnel records. Only 554 rows -- a pointer/catalog layer, not the full underlying record sets. Carries FIPS for geographic joins. Raw landing, all text.

National Archives records about Japanese Americans forcibly relocated and interned during World War II: name, age, sex, citizenship status, family number, and the relocation camp, tied to a county FIPS. A primary-source window into a government mass-detention program. Heads up: this is a thin 36-row slice, not the full series -- good for seeing the shape, not for counting people.
A sampler of NASA's public APIs: which API, the request, and the response metadata with links. 54 rows landed as a capability probe -- a menu of what NASA offers rather than a dataset in itself.

Every AIS broadcast from vessels in US waters across 2024 -- 7.3 million position reports with location, speed, heading, vessel name, type, and cargo. Ships are legally required to broadcast this, so it's the raw movement history of maritime traffic. Keyed by MMSI and IMO, so you can follow a specific ship over time or cross it with sanctions and ownership lists to spot dark or evasive vessels. Published by NOAA's Office for Coastal Management.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

NOAA's event-by-event record of US extreme weather: what happened (tornado, flood, heat, etc), where (lat/lon and FIPS), and the human and economic toll -- fatalities, injuries, and property/crop damage. The granular impact layer that disaster declarations miss. Heads up: damage amounts are text with K/M/B suffixes ('2.5K', '10.00M') that must be parsed, and CZ_TYPE='Z' rows are NWS forecast zones, not counties -- don't blindly join those to county FIPS. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

A snapshot of active NWS weather alerts from the weather.gov API: event type, severity, certainty, urgency, and the area description. It's a point-in-time capture (287 alerts), not a running archive -- useful as a live-feed schema and for joining weather context to events by area.

Award records from the NSF: title, awardee institution, PI, program officer, amount, and dates. A 125-row probe of the search API. Institution names match to universities across the Library; the full feed is worth a deeper pour.

Facility-level nursing home data compiled by the Long Term Care Community Coalition from CMS sources: certified beds, staffing levels, ownership type and detail, inspections, and penalties. Overlaps the official NURSING_HOMES table but adds the watchdog's ownership-detail angle -- CCN joins the two.

The OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list -- 19,115 rows of people, entities, and vessels the U.S. Treasury has sanctioned, plus the program (Iran, Russia, narcotics, terrorism, etc.) that got them listed. Vessel rows carry a 7-digit IMO number, so you can tie a sanctioned ship to its movements. Raw landing: every value is stored as text exactly as published.

Cleaned record of U.S. Supreme Court cases from the Oyez archive -- each row is one case with the parties (petitioner vs. respondent), the lower court, argument and decision dates, the disposition, who wrote the majority, and a per-justice vote breakdown. It also links to the oral-argument audio and full transcript. Keyed by docket number and case name; strong for tracing how a justice ruled across cases. Heads up: this table holds 25 cases -- a slice of the 1955-present archive, good for seeing the shape, not a full census of the Court's docket.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Statistical tables from the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation covering the single-employer and multiemployer insurance programs: financial position, claims, and benefit payments, in long metric format by year. Context table for pension-failure stories; pairs with RETIREMENT_PLAN_FILINGS.

Maps 406 political appointees in the federal executive branch to the corporate sectors they're tied to, flagging which are revolving-door cases (people moving between industry and the regulators that oversee it). Each row lists the person, their agency and role, and up to a dozen economic sectors of interest. Matching is by name only (probabilistic), so treat links as leads to verify, not proof. Compiled by the Revolving Door Project.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Loan-level records for the SBA's two big small-business programs, FOIA-released and updated quarterly: who borrowed, where they are, who lent, and how much. Borrower names and addresses make this a strong name/place-match table for tracing businesses.
Loan-level records of Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loans of $150,000 or more, including borrower, lender, amounts, and forgiveness status.

The gold-standard Supreme Court Database: one row per justice-vote across every case since 1946, with who won, the legal issue, the direction (liberal/conservative), and who wrote the majority. 83,644 rows, cleaned and analytics-ready. This is how you study how a justice actually voted, not just what they said. Keyed by docket number.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Filing-level metadata from the SEC's structured JSON API: who filed (CIK, EIN, entity name), which form, when, and links to documents. A 200-row probe -- the bigger sibling SEC_EDGAR_FILINGS on this shelf carries 49K rows from the full-text side. Both carry CIK, the steel join key of corporate America.

A crosswalk from public companies to their SEC identifiers -- each row maps a company name to its CIK (the SEC's permanent filer ID) and its stock ticker. It's small but load-bearing: the CIK is how you jump from a ticker like AAPL to that company's SEC filings and everything else keyed on CIK. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by CIK; ~10,414 rows.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

One row per financial statement filing to the SEC: the filer's name, CIK, EIN, industry code (SIC), addresses, fiscal period, and form type (10-K, 10-Q, etc.). The index to public companies' financials -- join out to the actual line-item numbers by accession number (ADSH). Raw as loaded (all text); carries CIK and EIN as join keys. From SEC DERA.

SlaveVoyages Intra-American database -- one row per documented voyage (ship, captain, owners, ports, dates, counts). Clean projection over current landing; wide historical source, all fields kept as text.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)
Voyage-level dataset of transatlantic slave trading expeditions, including ships, nationalities, ports, dates, and enslaved-person counts embarked/disembarked.

What it actually costs Uncle Sam to borrow: the average interest rate on US Treasury debt, month by month, broken out by security type (bills, notes, bonds, savings bonds, etc.). Cleaned and analytics-ready, 4,961 rows going back decades. Useful for tracking how the government's interest burden shifts over time. No cross-source join keys -- it's a time series, not an entity table.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

The official daily total of US national debt outstanding, down to the penny, broken into debt held by the public versus intragovernmental holdings (money the government owes itself). One row per business day -- the raw time series behind every 'national debt' chart. Cleaned and analytics-ready; no join key, it's a standalone daily series; ~8,329 rows.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

6.3 million federal prime contract transactions (Oct 2024-Sep 2025): the awarding agency, the company (with UEI/DUNS/CAGE IDs and parent company), dollar amounts, work description, industry code, and even top-officer pay. The core follow-the-money table for government spending, keyed by UEI/DUNS/NAICS/FIPS so it joins to companies and places. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

Every top-tier federal agency from USAspending.gov with current fiscal-year budget authority, dollars obligated, dollars actually paid out (outlays), and each agency's share of the total federal budget. Only 111 rows -- the high-level scoreboard of who controls what money. Joins to detailed spending by agency name. Raw landing, all text.

Quarterly USCIS statistics per form type (green cards, naturalization, asylum, work permits): how many filed, approved, denied, pending, and how long they take. The backlog table -- 'how long does form X take now vs. 2020' lives here.

Statistical tables from the Administrative Office of the US Courts covering appellate, district, and bankruptcy caseloads. Landed as table-level rows (50 of them) rather than case-level data -- fine for 'how busy is this district' context, not for tracking individual cases.

The full USGS catalog of every earthquake magnitude 2.5 and up: when it hit, exactly where (lat/lon), how deep, how strong, and a plain-language place name. 443,274 events across the whole history the survey tracks. Joins to anything geographic by lat/lon. Raw landing, values stored as text; from the US Geological Survey.

USGS mineral resources data: who produces how much of which commodity, reserves, rank, and how import-reliant the US is -- including critical minerals. Country and commodity by year make this the reference table for supply-chain and resource-leverage questions.

Catalog records for USGS's scanned historical topo maps: title, creation/publication dates, file format, and download URL. A finding aid for 'what did the terrain look like then' -- 250 rows probed from a much larger collection.

Readings from the USGS national water monitoring network: site, parameter (streamflow, gauge height, temperature...), timestamp, and value, with state/county codes and coordinates. 6.7 million rows of real instrument data -- the backbone for any drought, flood, or contamination timeline.

Company filings from SEC EDGAR: entity name, CIK, ticker, form type (10-K, 8-K, 13F...), filing date, SIC industry code, and state of incorporation. The most-connected corporate table in the Library -- CIK and EIN join it to financial statements, tickers, and nonprofit records; SIC links it to industry tables.

Award-level federal spending from the USAspending REST API: recipient (with UEI/DUNS/EIN), awarding agency, award type, and obligated vs. outlaid dollars. Only a 300-row probe has landed -- the full firehose is enormous and comes later. Recipient IDs make this joinable to contractors, nonprofits, and sanctions lists.

The VA's National Veteran Suicide report appendix: veteran suicide death counts and adjusted rates broken out by sex over 2001-2023. The authoritative federal number on veteran suicide. Heads up: this is a raw spreadsheet dump (144 rows) -- the real column headers are buried in the data (columns are named COL_1..COL_12) and need reshaping in staging before it's usable. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

The standard ideology measure (DW-NOMINATE) for every member of Congress in every Congress: a two-dimensional score placing each member on the liberal-conservative spectrum, plus basic bio. Keyed by ICPSR ID so it links to the Congress member spine. This is the small member-level file; the full member-by-vote matrix lives separately. Raw landing, stored as text; 51,061 rows from Voteview/UCLA.

The full member-by-vote matrix from Voteview: one row per (member, roll-call) with how they voted (cast code), across the whole history of Congress. This is the raw fuel for missed-votes, party-unity, and vote-similarity stats. Members key on ICPSR id. Heads up: raw landing (every value text) -- it's the vote grid, not the bill text or vote descriptions.

One row per congressional roll-call vote (3,364 rows): the chamber, date, the question being voted on, the bill number, yea and nay counts, and whether it passed. This is the context and denominator for the member-by-member vote matrix -- what was voted on and how it came out. Keyed by congress+chamber+roll number. Raw text landing (Voteview / UCLA).

The Library of Congress 'Born in Slavery' collection: interviews with formerly enslaved people conducted by the Federal Writers' Project, 1936-1938 -- the person's name, the interviewer, the date and state, and the full text of the account. Keyed to state FIPS so it maps geographically. A primary historical record in the people's own words; this table holds 100 items.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Project records and indicators from the Asian Development Bank: project name, country, sector, approval date, and loan amounts. Small (41 rows) but real -- pairs with the sovereign-debt and procurement tables for who-finances-what-in-Asia questions.
Dataset catalog from datos.gob.ar with titles, organizations, formats, and licenses, plus some sampled time-series values. A finding aid for Argentine government data.
Meant to hold Australasian and global case law and legislation records from AustLII. One row landed -- a schema probe. Re-pour before use.
A 10-row probe of dados.gov.br's dataset catalog: title, organization, theme, and resource links. Placeholder coverage -- the full catalog needs a re-pour.

Switzerland's central business-name index: registered Swiss companies with their UID number, legal form, status, address and canton. Full source is the whole country, but only 18 rows landed here -- treat it as a preview for exploring the columns, not a count of Swiss firms. Carries name/address/country for probabilistic joins to other corporate data. Raw text landing (Swiss Federal Registry of Commerce).

Ecuador's national public procurement, 2015 to today: which government agency bought something, which company won it, and the dollar amounts at each stage (tender, award, signed contract). Standard follow-the-money for public spending -- spot the same suppliers winning over and over. Matching to companies is by name only (no clean ID), so cross-source links are probabilistic, not exact.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)
Time-series indicators from Egypt's national statistics portal: indicator name, category, year, value. A 150-row probe kept for international coverage breadth.

Ember's global electricity dataset: for 200+ countries and regions, the yearly numbers on how power is generated (coal, gas, wind, solar, etc.), plus capacity, emissions, imports, and demand. 118,463 rows in long format with year-over-year change built in. The go-to for tracking the clean-energy transition country by country. Keyed by country (with ISO codes) for easy geographic joins.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Records from the Ensembl REST API: species, assembly, region, feature type, and gene symbols. A 643-row probe demonstrating the API. Far from the Library's accountability core -- parked here in case a bio-adjacent story ever needs it.

Spanish BORME company filings -- one row per registry act (company, act type, province, CVE, PDF). Recovered from landing (was frozen at 3 rows).  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Document-level records from the EU's official legal repository: CELEX identifier, document type, author institution, dates, and whether it's in force. A 53-row probe of the API. The CELEX/ELI/ECLI identifier columns are the join keys of the EU legal world.

Indicator observations from Eurostat's SDMX API: dataflow, country, period, and value. A 450-row probe demonstrating the pipe. The country codes join to any ISO-keyed international table; specific indicators need targeted pours.

The EU's official consolidated sanctions list: subject type, names/aliases, programme, and legal-basis references, maintained daily by the European Commission. The European counterpart to OFAC's list -- run any name of interest against both; entity records here match to companies and vessels elsewhere in the Library.

An index of Europol's flagship strategic reports on serious organized crime (SOCTA) and cybercrime (IOCTA): title, year, language, and download link. It's a small document index (26 reports), there for provenance when an investigation cites European threat assessments.

Meant to hold FAO's global food, agriculture, and trade statistics. Four rows of raw content landed -- a dead probe, not data. Needs a proper re-pour against the FAOSTAT bulk endpoints before it's anything.

The FAO's baseline food-security series: prevalence of undernourishment, food-insecurity experience scales, and dietary energy supply, by country and year (279k rows over 60+ years). This is slow-moving structural hunger -- the backdrop that acute famine spikes sit on top of. Country is FAO's M49 'Area Code'; map to ISO3 to join, and filter out the mixed-in aggregate rows ('World', 'Africa'). Raw text landing (FAO).

FATF mutual-evaluation ratings: country, recommendation, rating, and evaluation round across technical compliance and effectiveness. The 'how leaky is this jurisdiction' reference -- context for any cross-border money trail.

The annual freedom scorecard: each country rated on political rights and civil liberties (2013-2024), broken into the A1-G4 sub-indicators that build the score -- the standard evidence for a democratic-backsliding story. 2,723 rows (country x year). Heads up: no ISO country code, so you need a name-to-country crosswalk to join it cleanly, and commercial reuse is restricted. Raw landing, all text.
Dataset-level catalog of data.gouv.fr: what France publishes, who publishes it, license, and update dates. A finding aid -- use it to spot French datasets worth pouring, not as data itself.

Event records from GDELT 2.0, which scans world news every 15 minutes and codes events: actors, event codes, locations, and tone. A 1,015-row probe of a firehose that produces millions of rows daily. Powerful for timelines once poured at scale; treat machine-coded events as leads, not facts.

Peak-ground-acceleration hazard values from the Global Earthquake Model's mosaic of national seismic models. Only a 12-row probe landed -- enough to see the shape (lat/lon, PGA at 10% in 50 years), not enough to map. Re-pour before using.
A single-row probe of data.gov.ge. Schema only -- nothing to query yet.

Country-level estimates of illicit financial flows from trade misinvoicing, as published by Global Financial Integrity. Small (25 rows) and estimate-based -- context numbers for money-laundering stories, not evidence.
A 10-row probe of data.gov.gh: dataset title, ministry, format, and links. Placeholder coverage for West Africa; re-pour for the full catalog.

One row per documented killing, disappearance, or attack on a land/environmental defender: name, country, year, sector (mining, logging, agribusiness...), and alleged perpetrator type. Compiled by Global Witness -- grim, careful data that pairs with mining and land-deal tables.

Greece's General Electronic Commercial Registry: registered Greek companies with their GEMI number, tax ID (AFM), legal form, status, and formation/closure dates. Only 40 rows landed, so this is a preview for exploring the columns, not a real count of Greek firms. Joins to other corporate data by company name (probabilistic). Raw text landing (Central Union of Chambers of Greece).

Case-law from the European Court of Human Rights -- each row is a judgment or decision naming the person, the respondent country, which Convention article was at stake, and whether the court found a violation. Good for tracking how governments are held to account on human rights. Heads up: this is a thin sample (2,000 rows), not the full HUDOC database -- use it to explore the shape of the data, not to count cases. Keyed by country and case name.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

The official famine-tracking data (IPC): how many people fall into each hunger phase -- from stressed up to Phase 5, Famine -- for a country and analysis window. Each row is one phase for one country/date, with the head count and the share of the population it represents. This is the data behind 'famine confirmed' headlines. Country is an ISO3 code. Raw landing table: every value stored as text, exactly as loaded, so cast the numbers before you do math on them.

Italy's official statistics as individual observations -- 56,096 data points spanning the economy, labor, trade, demographics, and environment, pulled from Istat's SDMX web services. Each row is one measured value with its dataflow, dimensions, time period, and unit. It's a long, machine-readable time-series store, not a friendly summary table -- you filter by dataflow and dimensions to get a specific indicator. Published by Istat, Italy's national statistics institute.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

An academic dataset (Harvard Dataverse) cataloging Russian covert and hybrid operations against Europe: what happened, where, the event category, the apparent goal, and the target type. The evidence base for Russia-NATO gray-zone conflict reporting. Heads up: 153 hand-coded incidents -- an analyst-curated set, not a comprehensive registry, and the coding categories are judgment calls. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

The authoritative chronology of every North Korean missile flight test from 1984 to today: missile name and type (SRBM/ICBM/etc), date and time, geocoded launch facility (lat/lon), apogee, distance, and whether it succeeded. Built for tracking the pace and reach of the DPRK missile program. Heads up: many 'numeric' fields (apogee, distance, landing location) are free text including 'Unknown' -- kept as text here, parse in staging. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

OpenSanctions' consolidated global sanctions list: 71,011 targets -- people, companies, and vessels sanctioned by governments and bodies around the world -- with names, aliases, birth dates, countries, addresses, identifiers, and which sanction programs hit them. The starting point for 'who's blacklisted' and cross-checking who's still doing business. Raw landing, stored as text.

Annual military spending for every country in constant US dollars, sourced from SIPRI via Our World in Data. Carries ISO-3 country codes, so it joins to any country-keyed source in the Library -- built for comparing spending trajectories (China vs US vs Taiwan, etc). Heads up: some rows are regional aggregates (tagged '(SIPRI)') that you filter out for country-level work, and only this one metric (constant USD) is here -- %GDP and per-capita live in sibling tables. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

The gold-standard conflict backbone: individual events of organized violence (war, insurgency, one-sided killings) with a date, lat/lon, the two sides, and best/low/high fatality estimates because exact death counts are uncertain. Map it, count it, or track a war over time. Raw as loaded (all text); has lat/lon for spatial joins, no country ID key. UCDP GED Global v251.

For each pair of countries and year, how closely they voted together at the UN General Assembly, plus each side's 'ideal point' (where it sits on a global alignment scale). The standard academic measure of who's diplomatically in whose camp. Raw as loaded (all text); countries identified by ccode, no standard join key. Voeten data via Harvard Dataverse.

The World Bank's International Debt Statistics: developing-country external debt -- stocks and debt service -- with a rare creditor-by-creditor breakdown showing who each country actually owes (bilateral, multilateral, private). The core source for the global debt crisis. Keyed by ISO-3 country code plus a counterpart (creditor) code; filter counterpart to WLD for a clean all-creditors country panel. Heads up: only low- and middle-income countries (no G7 debtors), years run wide (1970-2032) and 2025+ are projections/nulls. Wide format -- one column per year. Raw as loaded (text).
