A deep coding of U.S. state marijuana policy by state and year: whether medical and recreational use were approved and implemented, how it happened (ballot measure, legislature, court), plus dozens of fine-grained rules -- home growing, dispensary limits, taxes, testing, possession penalties, caregiver rules. Distinguishes 'approved' from 'implemented' throughout, so you can see the gap between passing a law and enforcing it. Keyed by state and FIPS. Raw landing table: values stored as text (including some scored/z-scored policy indices), and note a couple of unlabeled COL_* placeholder columns from the source.

Metadata for preprint papers -- early research posted on bioRxiv and medRxiv before formal peer review -- including title, authors, correspondence institution, funder, license, and how many times each was viewed or downloaded. Also tracks whether a preprint later got published in a journal and how long that took. Useful for following who funds what science and how fast findings spread. Cleaned and analytics-ready; ~432 rows here.  (Raw as-loaded copy; the cleaned version is in LIBRARY_MARTS.)

Guttmacher's monthly estimate of abortions in each US state -- a median plus a lower and upper bound, because these are modeled estimates, not a hard count. The go-to for tracking how state bans shifted where abortions happen. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key, matched on state name. Treat the numbers as estimates with error bars, not exact totals.

The Judicial Common Space (JCS) lifetime ideology score for US Courts of Appeals judges, placed on the same left-right scale used for Congress. 705 rows, one per judge with name, circuit, and score. Lets you ask whether a case landed before a liberal or conservative bench. Heads up: raw landing (text-as-loaded) with no clean join key -- match to judges by name/circuit.

The academic 'where does the median voter sit' series, one row per year (102 total) on a single common scale so you can compare the Supreme Court to Congress to the White House on the same yardstick. Circuit medians plus standard deviations for all 13 appeals circuits show how liberal or conservative each bench leans over time. Raw landing table (Judicial Common Space, Wash U. St. Louis) -- every value stored as text, cast before you do math.

The Judicial Common Space (JCS) ideology score for each Supreme Court justice, on the same DW-NOMINATE scale as Congress, one row per (justice, term) from 1937 to 2022. Tracks how a justice's placement -- and the Court's overall tilt -- shifted over time. 782 rows. Raw landing, stored as text; match to justices by name.

A record of North Korean missile flight tests: date, missile type, launch facility, apogee, distance flown, bearing, and whether it succeeded. Good for mapping impact points and tracking escalation. This is a derived/enriched mirror (from CNS/NTI data), not the primary source -- treat missile and facility values as codes needing a lookup. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key.

A one-number-per-year tally of reported AI incidents and controversies, from the AI Incident Database via Stanford's AI Index. Just enough to draw the 'AI harms are accelerating' trend line. Heads up: this is a rolled-up annual count (14 rows), not the underlying incidents -- use it as a headline chart or sanity check, not for digging into what actually happened. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text).

For each country and year, its total annual CO2 emissions -- the core number behind who's driving climate change and how that's shifted over time. Note this is total emissions, not per-person. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key, matched on country name/code. From Our World in Data.

For every country and year, its Corruption Perceptions Index score -- how corrupt its public sector is seen to be by experts and business people. A perception score, not a count of actual crimes, so read it as reputation. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key, matched on country name/code. From Our World in Data / Transparency International.

The total fertility rate (average children born per woman) for every country over time, from Our World in Data. The demographic engine behind aging and population-decline stories. Carries ISO-3 country codes, so it joins to any country-keyed source in the Library. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text) -- includes regional/aggregate 'entity' rows alongside individual countries.

For every country and year, what percent of primary energy came from coal, oil, and gas. The single clearest number for how far off fossil fuels a country still is. Raw as loaded (all text) -- cast the year and percent before charting. From Our World in Data; no join key, matched on country name/code.

Income inequality measured by the Gini index, by country and year (Our World in Data). Gini runs 0 (everyone earns the same) to 1 (one person has it all), so a single row tells you how lopsided a country's income was in a given year, tagged with world region. Country is an ISO3 code for joining. Raw landing table -- values stored as text; cast the coefficient before comparing. Coverage varies by country and year, so it's uneven, not a complete grid.

The homicide rate (killings per 100,000 people) for every country over time, sourced from UNODC via Our World in Data. The standard way to compare violence across countries and track it over time. Carries ISO-3 country codes, so it joins to any country-keyed source in the Library. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text) -- includes regional/aggregate 'entity' rows alongside individual countries.

For each country and year, how many years a newborn can expect to live -- the single best summary of a population's overall health. Great for long-run trends and comparing countries. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key, matched on country name/code. From Our World in Data.

Estimated nuclear warhead counts for the nine weapons states (US, Russia, China, France, UK, India, Pakistan, Israel, North Korea) plus South Africa and a World total, tracked over time. Great scene-setting for the global arsenal race, keyed by country ISO-3 code. Heads up: this is weapons-states only -- Iran is NOT in it, so it's context, not Iran data. Raw landing table, values stored as text.

Refugee counts by country of origin and year (Our World in Data / UNHCR): each row says how many people from a given country were living as refugees that year, tagged with world region. It answers 'where are people fleeing from, and how has that grown?' Country is an ISO3 code for joining to other international data. Raw landing table -- values stored as text, so cast the count before summing.

Global temperature anomaly by year (Our World in Data): how much warmer or cooler each year was versus a long-run baseline, with upper and lower uncertainty bounds. This is the classic warming curve -- the closer you get to today, the higher the anomaly. Entity is usually 'World' but region rows exist. Raw landing table -- values stored as text; cast the average and bounds before plotting the trend.

For each country and year, the number of people killed in terrorist attacks. Good for tracking where and when terrorism spikes; what counts as 'terrorism' is a definitional call made by the source, so compare carefully. Raw as loaded (all text); no join key, matched on country name/code. From Our World in Data.

A global tracker of ransomware attacks: which organization got hit, by which gang, in what sector and country, and when. The broadest worldwide view of who's under attack, including critical infrastructure like healthcare and energy. Heads up: victim names are scraped from criminal leak sites and claimed by the attackers -- unverified, with duplicate/typo'd org names and loosely-mapped sectors, so clean before you count. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text); no firm ID, so cross-source matching is by name.

The Vera Institute's county-level record of who's locked up in America: jail and prison populations, admissions, and rates over decades, split by race and sex. The spine of mass-incarceration reporting. Keyed by county FIPS, so it joins to almost any US geographic data. Heads up: not every county reports every year, so coverage is patchy across the time series. Raw as loaded (every value stored as text) -- and it's very wide, with hundreds of demographic breakdown columns.

The Washington Post's incident-level record of people shot and killed by US police: name, age, race, date, city/county/state, lat/lon, and the agency (via AGENCY_IDS). The standard citable source for police-violence reporting. Heads up: fatal SHOOTINGS only -- it excludes Tasers, in-custody deaths, and vehicle deaths, so it undercounts total police killings. Raw as loaded (text); AGENCY_IDS is a delimited list that needs unnesting to name the agency, and lat/lon are often block-level.

Every Internet Archive capture of the DOJ Epstein Library listing pages since Nov 2025 -- one row per snapshot with timestamp, HTTP status, and a content digest. When the digest changes between captures, the page changed, attested by a third party -- reconstructing edits from before anyone was actively watching. 1.5M rows, all packed in a single RECORD text column. Raw landing, all text.

A grab of 2,542 Department of Justice web pages as they were saved on the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine -- useful for catching what DOJ published and later changed or deleted. Raw landing: each row is one page's captured text in a single RECORD field, no structure or join keys yet. Good for full-text digging, not for clean tabular analysis.

A capture of Department of Justice web pages as archived by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine -- each row is one snapshot record, useful for proving what DOJ said on its site at a given moment and catching pages that were later changed or removed. No documented publisher or URL metadata on this table, and the whole payload sits in a single RECORD column. Raw landing table: stored exactly as scraped (text), so you'll need to parse the RECORD field to pull out URLs and timestamps.

The top 100 US companies ranked by revenue, with industry, revenue growth, employee count, and headquarters. A quick who's-who of American corporate giants, useful as a starting reference to join out to contracts, filings, and lobbying by company name. Heads up: only 100 rows, scraped from Wikipedia, and the only join key is company NAME (fuzzy). Raw landing table, values stored as text.
Foreign Agent Registration Act (FARA) filings — who lobbies for foreign governments. One row per registration event, keyed by registration number. Curated mart table with typed columns.
Ireland Companies Registration Office — all Irish registered companies. Curated mart table (818K+ records).

The complete IRS Business Master File of tax-exempt organizations: every nonprofit, foundation, church group, and association the IRS recognizes -- 3.9 million of them, with EIN, address, exemption subsection, and ruling date. This is the spine table for anything nonprofit: start here, then hang 990 financials, revocations, and grants off the EIN.

The master list of every US county and county-equivalent -- 3,222 of them -- each with its FIPS code (the standard geographic ID that joins to almost any US dataset), state, 2020 population, and a lat/lon population-center point. This is a lookup/reference table: when you have a county code and want a name, population, or a point to map, you land here. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

A plain calendar table -- one row for every single day across ~86 years -- pre-broken into year, quarter, month, day-of-week, weekend flag, and US fiscal year. It doesn't hold any real-world events; it's the spine you join other data to so you can group by month, filter weekends, or roll up to fiscal year without recomputing dates every time. Standard analytics helper table.

The clean reference table for all 56 US states and territories -- FIPS code, two-letter USPS abbreviation, full name, and whether it's a territory. This is a building-block lookup: join it to give any dataset with a state FIPS code a proper state name. Small by design; it's infrastructure, not a story.

Every census tract in the US -- 85,391 small neighborhood-sized areas -- with its GEOID, county and state FIPS, 2020 population, and a population-weighted center point (lat/lon). This is a dimension table: the geographic spine that almost every place-based dataset joins to. Use it to roll neighborhood data up to counties or states, or to map anything that carries a tract ID. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

A crosswalk mapping ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTA5) to the counties they fall in -- 46,960 rows because ZIPs often straddle county lines. Its job is to translate anything reported by ZIP into county FIPS so it joins to census, health, and justice data. Core plumbing for making geographic data line up; check the vintage since boundaries shift over time.

History table tracking the size of Epstein-related document collections over time -- 339 captures recording, for each page, how many files it appeared to hold at each moment (from the site's own pager). It exists to detect documents being quietly added or removed. This is change-detection metadata, not the documents; the file counts are estimates read off the page.

Monitoring table for a targeted Epstein investigation -- 619 document files being tracked across sources, with each file's URL, dataset name, and when it was first and last observed. Its job is to catch when files appear, change, or vanish from the public record. This is a surveillance/provenance ledger of the documents, not the document contents themselves.

A change-log built from Wayback Machine (web archive) captures -- each row is one snapshot of a tracked URL, flagging what happened since the last capture: page added, content changed, went offline (404), or came back. It stores content fingerprints so you can prove a page's text actually changed, and when. Built for the Epstein investigation to catch quietly scrubbed or edited pages. Cleaned and analytics-ready; ~203K rows.
Index of finding candidates in this schema. Each is a LEAD (exact-ID match or defensible model/screen), not a published claim. Live row counts.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). OIG-excluded providers (LEIE) listed as affiliated with a Medicare-enrolled facility (CMS Facility Affiliation, NPI->CCN). Exact NPI match; NPI=0000000000 excluded. Who gets hurt: patients at facilities staffed by federally-excluded providers. Built 2026-07-23. Sources: FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE x FED_CMS_FACILITY_AFFILIATION. Caveat: affiliation file is partially loaded - counts will grow when fully poured.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). OIG-excluded providers (LEIE) who received reportable industry payments (CMS Open Payments) in a program year AFTER their exclusion date. Exact NPI match; the year gate removes pre-exclusion history so remaining payments post-date the ban. Who gets hurt: patients/taxpayers (excluded providers should be out of federally-reimbursed care). Built 2026-07-23. Sources: FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE x FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS(+2022/2023). NPI=0000000000 excluded (LEIE libel trap).

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). The "trapped patients" layer on FINDINGS.EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION: OIG-excluded providers who received industry payments in a program year AFTER their exclusion (sound temporal gate via Open Payments PROGRAM_YEAR), enriched with whether the provider's LEIE-address county is a HRSA-Designated health shortage area (patients have few/no alternatives). Who gets hurt: patients in underserved areas still exposed to federally-excluded providers who remain financially active in the drug/device economy. Exact NPI throughout. CAVEAT: county derived from the excluded provider's LEIE mailing address ZIP (practice-location proxy). Built 2026-07-27. Sources: FINDINGS.EXCLUDED_PROVIDER_PAID_AFTER_EXCLUSION x FED_HHS_OIG_LEIE(zip) x geo crosswalk x FED_HRSA_SHORTAGE_AREAS.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). Companies that (1) hold federal contracts (USASpending, by recipient/parent UEI) AND (2) own EPA facilities that are significant non-compliers or have been penalized (EPA ECHO: FAC_SNC_FLG / FAC_TOTAL_PENALTIES / formal actions), bridged by the EPA->corporate crosswalk (EPA_REGISTRY_ID -> PARENT_UEI, MATCH_CONFIDENCE>=0.80). Who gets hurt: taxpayers/public - federal dollars flowing to companies actively breaking environmental law. COVERAGE CAVEAT: strongly gated by the crosswalk, which currently resolves only ~6,886 EPA facilities to a parent UEI (681 at high confidence) out of millions - so this is a FLOOR, not the full picture; the count grows as the entity-resolution crosswalk is enriched. Exact UEI join on the contract side; crosswalk match is probabilistic (confidence-scored). Built 2026-07-27. Sources: FED_EPA_ECHO x XC_EPA_CORPORATE_CROSSWALK x FED_USASPENDING_CONTRACTS.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). Forward-looking closure-risk map: Medicare-participating hospitals (latest fiscal year per CCN in CMS HCRIS cost reports) that run a NEGATIVE operating margin (NET_INCOME_FROM_SERVICE_TO_PATIENTS / NET_PATIENT_REVENUE) and/or depend heavily on Medicaid revenue (NET_REVENUE_FROM_MEDICAID share), enriched with rural status and whether the hospital county is a HRSA-Designated shortage area. Who gets hurt: patients (especially rural/shortage-area) who lose their only hospital if Medicaid funding is cut. This is a RISK model on public financial filings, NOT a prediction of specific closures - a hospital can be unprofitable for years without closing. risk_tier: critical = negative margin + Medicaid-dependent(>20%) + (rural OR shortage county); high = negative margin + Medicaid-dependent; elevated = one risk factor. Amounts are single-year cost-report figures (cast from text). Built 2026-07-27. Source: FED_CMS_HCRIS x geo crosswalk x FED_HRSA_SHORTAGE_AREAS.
State rollup of FINDINGS.HOSPITAL_CLOSURE_RISK - the map layer. Counts of at-risk hospitals by state and risk tier. LEAD data, human review required before publication.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). Members of Congress ranked by campaign money (PAC + outside spending FOR them, summed across available cycles) against their legislative productivity (bills enacted, bills advanced past committee, substantive bills sponsored) and floor-vote attendance (missed-vote %). Surfaces the "paid, but low output / high absenteeism" quadrant. Keyed by BIOGUIDE. This is a screening lead, NOT an accusation - low bill counts can reflect committee/leadership role, seniority, or minority status; a human must judge context. CAVEAT: money is summed across cycles and output across congresses, so multi-term members accumulate more of both; treat money_pctile as relative standing, not causation. Built 2026-07-27. Sources: POLITICS__MEMBER_PAC_MONEY x POLITICS__MEMBER_BILL_RECORD x POLITICS__MEMBER_VOTING_RECORD.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review before publication). Medicare Part D prescribers who (1) received industry payments tied to opioid-ANALGESIC / pain products (CMS Open Payments 2022-2024) AND (2) are top-decile opioid prescribers WITHIN their own specialty (Part D OPIOID_PRSCRBR_RATE, percentile ranked per PRSCRBR_TYPE among prescribers with >=50 opioid claims). Exact NPI match on both sides; NPI 0000000000 and non-10-digit NPIs excluded. Who gets hurt: patients of high-volume opioid prescribers whose prescribing may be influenced by manufacturer money. IMPORTANT NUANCE: addiction-TREATMENT payments (Opioid Use Disorder, Opioid Overdose reversal, non-opioid analgesic) are EXCLUDED - those are the good guys; only pain/opioid-analgesic marketing counts. GEOGRAPHY CAVEAT: overdose_band_* columns come from CDC county drug-poisoning data that ENDS IN 2015 (pre-fentanyl era) and is banded into ranges - use as a persistence-of-geography signal only, NOT current death counts, and NOT as proof. Payment↔prescribing link is present-era and exact; the overdose band is a caveated enrichment, not a requirement. Built 2026-07-27. Sources: FED_CMS_PART_D_PRESCRIBERS x FED_CMS_OPEN_PAYMENTS(+2023,+2022) x geography crosswalk x FED_CDC_DRUG_POISONING_COUNTY.

State rollup of FINDINGS.OPIOID_PRESCRIBER_PAID_HIGH_RX - the map layer. Counts of flagged high-opioid prescribers who took opioid-analgesic industry money, and total such payments, by prescriber state. LEAD data - human review required before publication.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review). Committee-centric money-cluster map: for each FEC committee (PAC), how many distinct members of Congress it funded, split by party, and total dollars to each side. Surfaces PACs that fund substantial numbers of BOTH parties - the fingerprint of access-buying (spending for influence regardless of ideology) rather than ideological support. Exact IDs throughout: FED_FEC_COMMITTEE_TO_CANDIDATE (CMTE_ID->CAND_ID, positive contributions, excludes 24A independent-expenditure-AGAINST) -> POLITICS__MEMBER_FEC_ID (CAND_ID=FEC_ID -> BIOGUIDE, PARTY). both_sides_flag = funded >=5 Dems AND >=5 Reps. NOT an accusation - PACs legally give to both parties; this ranks WHO does it most and most evenly. Built 2026-07-27. Sources: FED_FEC_COMMITTEE_TO_CANDIDATE x POLITICS__MEMBER_FEC_ID x POLITICS__FEC_COMMITTEE.

FINDING CANDIDATE (lead, needs human review before publication). Orgs the IRS auto-revoked, never reinstated, yet still flagged DEDUCTIBILITY=1 in the IRS Business Master File. Exact EIN match. Who gets hurt: donors giving "deductible" money to orgs that lost 501(c) status. NUANCE: the long tail (small orgs) is the clean donor-harm story; high-revenue rows are often hospital/university reorganizations - review individually. Built/enriched 2026-07-23. Sources: FED_IRS_REVOCATION x FED_IRS_BMF.
State rollup of FINDINGS.REVOKED_BUT_DEDUCTIBLE - the map layer. Org counts + reported revenue by state for IRS-revoked, never-reinstated orgs still flagged tax-deductible.

One row per federal political committee per cycle -- campaign committees, PACs, party committees -- with its name, treasurer, location, type, party affiliation, and any connected organization or linked candidate. This is the roster of the entities that raise and spend federal political money. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by FEC committee ID (CMTE_ID), links to candidates via CAND_ID; ~40,945 rows.

The full history of federal judicial appointments -- each row is one judge's appointment to one court, with the nominating president and their party, nomination and confirmation dates, the Senate vote tally, and when they left. Follow it to see how presidents reshape the courts over decades. Cleaned and analytics-ready; keyed by the judge's National ID (NID); ~4,766 rows.

The biographical directory of federal judges from the Federal Judicial Center: one row per judge (4,067) with full name, birth and death years, gender, and race or ethnicity. This is the backbone that other court tables point back to -- appointments, ideology scores, and case rulings all identify judges by the IDs (NID/JID) living here. Cleaned and analytics-ready; if a federal judge existed, they're in this table.

A crosswalk linking 40 Supreme Court justices between two ID systems: the Supreme Court database's justice code and the Federal Judicial Center's judge ID (FJC_NID). It exists so a justice's voting record can join to their full biographical file. Includes how each match was made and a confidence flag -- a plumbing table, not an analysis in itself.

A single yearly scorecard placing all four power centers -- the President, the median House member, the median Senator, and the median Supreme Court justice -- on one common ideology scale (JCS/DW-NOMINATE style). 102 rows, one per year/term. Lets you see, at a glance, when the Court drifted away from the elected branches. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

One row per U.S. Court of Appeals judge with a Judicial Common Space (JCS) score -- a standard academic measure of where a judge sits on the liberal-to-conservative spectrum, derived from who appointed them. Includes the judge's name and circuit. Use it to ask whether a court's makeup tilts the outcomes it hands down; join by judge name to case or biography tables. Cleaned mart, analytics-ready; the score is an estimate, not a self-declared label.

One row per justice per term with their JCS ideology score -- a number that places each justice left-to-right and shows how they drifted over their career. 782 rows. Carries the SCDB justice code and the FJC judge ID so it joins to case votes and judge biographies. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

Breaks down the individual-donor side of each member of Congress's fundraising (1,057 rows) -- itemized giving, direct vs. earmarked (money bundled through groups like ActBlue/WinRed), self-contributions, and reattributions. Keyed by BIOGUIDE. Tells you not just how much a member raised from people, but how they raised it -- grassroots checks or funneled money. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

For each member of Congress each election cycle: how much PAC money they took, how many PACs gave, and how much outside groups spent to help or attack them. 1,258 rows. Keyed to the member via BIOGUIDE so it lines up with the member spine and crosswalk. The follow-the-money view of who's backing (and fighting) each legislator. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

One row per Supreme Court justice (40 total) with their term span, whether they're on the current bench, and counts of votes cast and cases heard. A small dimension table -- the roster you join to detailed vote records to see how each justice ruled. Good starting point for tracking the Court's makeup over time. Cleaned and analytics-ready.

The winner of every US federal election: office, year, state, district, the winner and their party, vote totals, share, and how close it was over the runner-up. Includes BIOGUIDE and ICPSR IDs so a winner links to their voting record and congressional profile. Cleaned outcomes built from MEDSL election data -- great for finding tight races and party flips.

IRS Business Master File (tax-exempt orgs) rolled to STATE x 501(c) SUBSECTION x NTEE_MAJOR (first letter of the NTEE code = broad nonprofit category). N_RECORDS = number of orgs; TOTAL_REVENUE = summed reported revenue. From 1.97M orgs.
IRS automatic revocations of tax-exempt status rolled to org STATE x REVOCATION_YEAR. N_RECORDS = number of revoked orgs. Revocation date parsed as DD-MON-YYYY. From 1.2M revocations.
NOAA Storm Events rolled to STATE x EVENT_YEAR x EVENT_TYPE. TOTAL_DEATHS/INJURIES = direct+indirect; DAMAGE columns parse the raw K/M/B/T suffix text into USD. From 1.78M events.
FCC ULS license records rolled to STATE x RADIO_SERVICE_CODE x LICENSE_STATUS x GRANT_YEAR. N_RECORDS = number of licenses. From 1.69M license records.
CMS Medicare provider utilization rolled to rendering-provider STATE x provider TYPE. TOTAL_SERVICES = total services; TOTAL_MEDICARE_PAYMENT = total Medicare paid USD. From 1.3M providers.

NPPES national provider registry rolled to primary TAXONOMY_CODE x practice STATE x ENTITY_TYPE_CODE (1=individual, 2=organization). N_RECORDS = number of NPIs. Join TAXONOMY_CODE to the NUCC taxonomy for specialty names. From 9.6M providers.

CMS Open Payments (industry payments to physicians/hospitals), 2022-2024 combined, rolled to paying MANUFACTURER/GPO x PROGRAM_YEAR x nature of payment. TOTAL_AMOUNT = total USD transferred. From ~43.3M raw payment rows.
CMS Open Payments 2022-2024 rolled to recipient SPECIALTY x PROGRAM_YEAR x recipient STATE. TOTAL_AMOUNT = total USD received. From ~43.3M raw payment rows.
CMS Medicare Part D prescribers rolled to prescriber STATE x prescriber TYPE (specialty). TOTAL_CLAIMS = total claims; TOTAL_DRUG_COST = total drug cost USD. From 1.42M prescribers.

FEC individual contributions rolled to recipient COMMITTEE (CMTE_ID) x CYCLE_YEAR. N_RECORDS = number of contributions; TOTAL_AMOUNT = total dollars raised. Join CMTE_ID to the FEC committee master for names. Junk years dropped. From 84.2M raw rows.

FEC individual contributions rolled to contributor STATE x CYCLE_YEAR (calendar year of the transaction). N_RECORDS = number of contributions; TOTAL_AMOUNT = total dollars. Junk transaction years (<1979 or >2026 in the raw) dropped. Pre-aggregated from 84.2M raw rows so it extracts under the 100k cap.
SBA 7(a)/504 loan approvals rolled to borrower STATE x PROGRAM x approval fiscal year. TOTAL_GROSS_APPROVAL = summed gross approved loan dollars. From 2.17M loans.

USASpending federal contract transactions rolled to AWARDING_AGENCY x NAICS_CODE (industry) x ACTION_YEAR. TOTAL_OBLIGATION = summed federal action obligation dollars (can be negative -- de-obligations). From 6.3M transactions.
USASpending federal contracts rolled to AWARDING_AGENCY x recipient STATE x ACTION_YEAR. TOTAL_OBLIGATION = summed federal obligation dollars. From 6.3M transactions.

One row per platform metric, derived live. Cite THIS in docs — never paste numbers into prose. Added 2026-07-02 (Fable audit: prose numbers rot, derived numbers survive).

Append-only audit log of human verdicts (who/when/what/why). The LATEST verdict per target wins. Corrections are NEW rows, never updates — the write role holds no UPDATE/DELETE. SMOKE_TEST row = permanent proof the wall holds.

The effective verdict per lead: COALESCE(lead-level, inherited cohort-level). SPECIFIC BEATS GENERAL — a lead decision always wins for that lead; the cohort verdict fills in only where no lead decision exists. DECISION_LEVEL says which applied. published can only ever appear at DECISION_LEVEL=lead (cohort verdicts cannot publish). Leads with no decision at either level are absent (readers COALESCE to pending).

Latest verdict per cohort (Pattern Desk; TARGET_KIND=cohort, TARGET_ID = naics||'|'||size_band). SMOKE_TEST excluded. Same append-only, latest-wins, deterministic tie-break semantics as V_LATEST_DECISIONS.

Latest verdict per lead (append-only means corrections are new rows; this view is the truth). SMOKE_TEST excluded. LEAD_ID aliased for the Reading Room app. Tie-break on DECISION_ID (deterministic) since 2026-08-01.
lead_id -> cohort_id (naics||'|'||size_band from frozen evidence) for the osha_cohort_outlier_2024 detector. The join spine of Pattern Desk decision inheritance.
